text:
incident-bot: PAGE: latency_slo.p95 exceeded in eu-west-1 routing group. auto-reroute to regional-fallback triggered. Affected routes: /v1/generate (models: rdx-large -> rdx-medium). Alerting SRE oncall.

alice_oncall: ack — i'm on it. grabbing logs and topology map.

bob_sre: seeing p95 jump ~2.1s -> 6.5s over last 6m for eu-west-1 primary. traffic shift to fallback region eu-north-1 started at t+00:02. Reroute churn: multiple flip-flops between regions every ~30-45s.

carol_runtime: investigating routing-controller logs. looks like the latency-slo policy has hysteresis set to 0s — it evaluates p95 window too aggressively. also noticed policy fallback_variant: "compatible" mapped to a heavier runtime variant in eu-north-1 which increases token latency.

kevin_ml: to add — model variant mapping: rdx-large in eu-west -> fallback set to rdx-medium in eu-north, but eu-north's rdx-medium is running quantized int8 kernels that actually increase latency for short-context workloads (weird perf regression).

dave_product: customer impact? are requests failing or just slow? any errors surfaced?

emma_custsuccess: monitoring prod-support queue — a few customers reporting slow responses in EU, no complete failures yet. SLA-impact likely in 15-30m if p95 stays elevated.

frank_ops: propose immediate mitigation: pause auto-reroute policy (temp), enable regional throttling + pin active variant to rdx-large in eu-west for known customers, then fix mapping/hysteresis.

alice_oncall: agree. step 1: disable routing-controller auto-reroute for eu-west-1 (manual only). step 2: set policy.hysteresis = 120s. step 3: override fallback_variant mapping for eu-north-1 to point to rdx-small-fast for short-context routes.

bob_sre: executing disable now: `curl -X POST "https://controlplane/api/v1/policies/auto_reroute/eu-west-1/disable" -H "Authorization: Bearer $INCIDENT_TOKEN"` -> 200 OK.

carol_runtime: applying hysteresis patch: ```
# patch
policy: latency-slo
window_seconds: 30
trigger_p95: 1.5
hysteresis_seconds: 120
```

carol_runtime: pushed config, controller picked up in ~9s. verifying no new reroutes in logs.

kevin_ml: pinned model variant for /v1/generate in eu-west-1: `rdx-large@v3.2.1` for routes matching short_context=true. This keeps latency characteristics stable.

frank_ops: also added temporary rate-limits for low-priority customers to reduce bursty load: policy updated.

emma_custsuccess: informing top-10 customers now (templated message): "We're seeing elevated response times in EU. We've applied routing protections and pinned model variants. We'll update in 15m."

dave_product: good. can we get a short postmortem action list? I want to include it in external incident summary if SLA breach occurs.

bob_sre: immediate action items: 1) keep auto-reroute disabled until policy hysteresis + mapping fixes validated, 2) telemetry alert: add rolling count of reroute events to detect flip-flop, 3) run perf test for rdx-medium in eu-north with short-context load, 4) revert quantized kernel usage for rdx-medium in eu-north if perf worse.

kevin_ml: i'll run perf tests now against eu-north rdx-medium with representative short-context workload. ETA 20m.

alice_oncall: handing off to night oncall @frank_ops — i'll stay reachable for 30m for context. frank, current state: auto-reroute disabled, hysteresis=120s, rdx-large pinned, fallback mapping temporarily changed, rate-limits applied, CS notified.

frank_ops: ack takeover. monitoring dashboards and logs. setting an incident timer: next status update at +15m.

incident-bot: note added to incident timeline: auto-reroute disabled by alice_oncall at ts=2060123468.

bob_sre: one more observation — the routing-controller health endpoint showed OOM-kicks in one controller pod in eu-west (oom_kill_count=3) around time of initial p95 spike. could be contributing to transient routing decisions. ops/infra should validate memory footprint.

carol_runtime: opened an infra ticket to increase controller JVM heap in eu-west autoscaler pool. also enabling verbose routing metrics for next 1h.

emma_custsuccess: updating customers: "We've applied mitigations and are monitoring. Next update in 15 minutes."

frank_ops: monitoring shows p95 trending down from 6.5s -> 2.0s after pinning and disabling reroute. still above SLO target (1.5s) but much better.

kevin_ml: perf test results: rdx-medium int8 in eu-north gives median ~80ms but p95 ~3.8s under short-context heavy load due to kernel cache thrash. confirmed regression. recommendation: don't use that variant as fallback for short-context routes.

bob_sre: plan: 1) rework fallback mapping so short-context routes fallback to rdx-small-fast (p95 1.2s), 2) add 2-minute hysteresis, 3) add metric alert: reroute_count > 3 in 5m -> suppress auto-reroute and page SRE.

alice_oncall: preparing incident summary for execs and legal: short description, customers impacted, actions taken, next steps, owners. will post when frank confirms stability.

frank_ops: stability looks good for now. leaving auto-reroute disabled until mapping + controller heap fix rolled out. handoff closed.

incident-bot: incident status: mitigation in progress. channel archived note pending final summary.

emma_custsuccess: after-action note for CS: keep support queue on priority watch for 3 hours and escalate any SLA claims to legal/sales ops.

carol_runtime: follow-up work items created: RUNTIME-472 (controller heap), ROUTE-893 (fallback mapping rules), PERF-221 (kernel regression triage).

alice_oncall: thanks team. I'll file the full postmortem template tonight. assign owners per the created tickets.

end of thread.
